dropped_from_p3.reason: Not a round 1 part, and not a fourth arrangement beside fitted, switchable and external. Two equal resistors in series with a capacitor from the centre tap to ground is a form of the fitted terminator. It is always on the bus and measures 120 Ohm across CANH and CANL, so the unpowered check still reads about 60 Ohm with both ends fitted (IOBoard.md:176). TCAN3413 SLLSFS8A section 8.2.1.1 offers it 'If filtering and stabilization of the common-mode voltage of the bus is desired' (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tcan3413.pdf, read 2026-09-29T01:00:32Z). The tree does not state whether the link needs common-mode filtering. The resistors and the capacitor are passives, which round 2 selects (Research.md Scope table; S2). P2's report already leaves the choice between one 120 Ohm and two 60 Ohm halves with a capacitor to round 2. The re-rank records P3's find as that round 2 option within the fitted choice.

P3's split terminator is a form of the fitted one. The resistor, and in the split form the two halves and the capacitor, are passives that round 2 selects (Research.md Scope table; S2 answer), so round 1 has no part and no LCSC number to record or verify for this function. The function stays without a part until the owner or the session accepts the arrangement as its round 1 result, or marks it 'not round 1'.

report.value: No function is added. Each CAN controller's crystal is a round 2 part: the Scope table puts 'crystals and inductors not fixed in round 1' in round 2, and round 1 fixes only the RP2354B's crystal. R2's share is the tolerance each controller's clock must hold. P2 carries it as a requirement of both controller functions and reports it per part: under +/-5,000 ppm on the link (V26) and +/-3,876 ppm on the external port (V27), temperature and ageing included. For the MCP2518FD it is a 40 or 20 MHz crystal or resonator, inside the part's own +/-0.5 % window (DS20006027B Table 7-3). The tree's MCP2515 driver takes a 16 MHz crystal (IOBoard.md:169).
